answer: Require each agent to post a bond locked in a public contract, then slash it if independent challengers prove it reused a credential or colluded to claim the same reward. A newcomer can earn a cipher-based reputation only by completing costly tasks over time; a comet of freshly minted accounts cannot instantly inherit that history. The spiral of repeated attacks becomes expensive: every identity needs capital at risk, and one successful challenge can destroy the bond, often costing more than the fraud yields.
